correctness.rationale: The square incidence matrix identity MM^T=(k-2)Id+2J and equal row and column sums give the dual pair counts. For k>=5, a distinct same-sort triple has all seven non-triple extension cells nonempty; the remaining cell is present iff its triple overlap t is 1. Each distinct same-sort pair permits both t values (choose inside one of its two common blocks but outside their intersection, or outside both); mixed triple cells stay nonempty after exclusions, and equalities are answered by the corresponding named object. Recursing on sets of extension types gives uniform rank-two pair types by atomic diagram, uniform rank-three singleton types by sort, and the common rank-four empty-tuple type. For rank three the four opposite-sort pair cells are all positive already at k>=4. The point outside a block pair separates k=3 at rank three; the rank-four formula asserting exactly one such point separates k=4, since u(k)=(k-2)(k-3)/2. The k=3 design is all 3-subsets of four points; at k=4 complementing blocks gives the unique Steiner triple system on seven points: label a noncollinear triple a,b,c and their pair completions d,e,f. For the seventh point g the remaining lines through a,b,c are respectively afg,beg,cdg, and the last line is def. For the Paley representative D={1,3,4,5,9} mod 11, the ten unordered pairs have circular distances 1 through 5 exactly twice each, giving the required directed difference multiplicities. Monotonicity of v(k) proves minimality within biplanes, not among arbitrary relational structures. Inspected both C++ sources and the recorded rank-three/rank-four transcripts; they compare four examples and were not executed or used as proof of the arbitrary-parameter conclusion.
